steps.title: Open Ads Manager
steps.description: Start guided setup from Meta Ads Manager, not from a generic chat.
steps.instruction: Open Meta Ads Manager and keep Spider visible.
steps.whyThisMatters: Spider needs the real screen to guide the setup step by step.
steps.riskIfWrong: If Spider cannot see the setup surface, it should ask for more context instead of guessing.
steps.recommendation: Open Meta Ads Manager and go to Campaigns.

steps.title: Create campaign
steps.description: Start a new campaign from the Ads Manager campaigns table.
steps.instruction: Click Create to start a new campaign.
steps.whyThisMatters: The campaign should be built from the Ad Mission, not from a platform default.
steps.riskIfWrong: Starting from the wrong surface can hide objective and setup choices Spider needs to review.
steps.recommendation: Click Create to start a new campaign.

steps.title: Choose recommended objective
steps.description: Select the objective recommended by the Campaign Direction.
steps.instruction: Choose the objective Spider recommended for this Ad Mission.
steps.whyThisMatters: The objective tells Meta what kind of outcome to optimize for.
steps.riskIfWrong: The campaign can optimize toward the wrong behavior, such as visits instead of buyers.
steps.recommendation: Choose the recommended objective from the Campaign Direction.

steps.title: Avoid Traffic for sales
steps.description: For a sales Ad Mission, Traffic is usually a mismatch because it can optimize for visits instead of buyer intent.
steps.instruction: Choose Sales. You are trying to sell, not collect cheap visits.
steps.whyThisMatters: Sales aligns optimization with purchase intent.
steps.riskIfWrong: Traffic can produce cheap clicks from people who are unlikely to buy.
steps.recommendation: Choose Sales for a sales Ad Mission. Do not choose Traffic unless the mission is explicitly visits or content distribution.

steps.title: Name campaign
steps.description: Name the campaign so the Ad Mission and later Decision Memory are easy to connect.
steps.instruction: Name the campaign after the offer, objective, and date.
steps.whyThisMatters: Clear naming makes later 72h review less messy.
steps.riskIfWrong: Generic names make it harder to compare decisions later.
steps.recommendation: Use a clear campaign name tied to the offer and objective.

steps.title: Review budget boundary
steps.description: Budget changes are a spend boundary and must remain manual.
steps.instruction: Keep the budget inside the planned range.
steps.whyThisMatters: Budget sets the speed of learning and the cost of mistakes.
steps.riskIfWrong: Increasing budget early can scale confusion instead of learning.
steps.nextAction: Continue only if the budget matches the Campaign Plan.
steps.recommendation: Review the planned budget and stop before increasing spend beyond the Ad Mission budget.

steps.title: Configure audience
steps.description: Use the Campaign Direction audience starting point instead of over-segmenting too early.
steps.instruction: Start with the planned audience and avoid splitting into too many ad sets.
steps.whyThisMatters: Small budgets need enough signal in one place.
steps.riskIfWrong: Too many audiences can starve every test and make the 72h review useless.
steps.recommendation: Use the planned audience starting point and avoid unnecessary fragmentation.

steps.title: Configure creative
steps.description: Use the planned creative angle and keep the ad promise aligned with the offer.
steps.instruction: Add the creative variation that matches the Campaign Plan.
steps.whyThisMatters: Creative qualifies the audience before settings do.
steps.riskIfWrong: A vague or mismatched creative can make good setup look broken.
steps.recommendation: Use the Campaign Plan creative angle and keep the promise specific.

steps.title: Configure tracking
steps.description: Select the conversion event that matches the mission before publishing.
steps.instruction: Choose the event from the Campaign Direction, such as Purchase or Lead.
steps.whyThisMatters: The campaign should optimize for the business event, not a vanity action.
steps.riskIfWrong: Bad tracking can make the 72h review useless or misleading.
steps.recommendation: Verify tracking and event selection before publishing.

steps.title: Stop before Publish
steps.description: Publishing is a spend and launch boundary. Spider must stop before launch and require manual user action.
steps.instruction: Do not publish inside Spider. Publishing is outside the current MVP.
steps.whyThisMatters: The user is about to spend money.
steps.riskIfWrong: Mistakes become live spend instead of a cheap correction.
steps.recommendation: Stop before publishing. The user may publish manually outside Spider if they choose.

steps.title: Preflight Audit Locked
steps.description: Preflight is a future safety gate and is not available in the current MVP.
steps.instruction: Do not present Preflight as available. Stop at the manual publish boundary.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the last cheap moment to catch expensive mistakes.
steps.riskIfWrong: The user may publish a misaligned campaign and pay to learn the obvious.
steps.recommendation: Preflight is locked. The MVP stops before publishing.
